newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money nudges higher ahead of month-end.
newsitem.headline: German call money nudges higher ahead of month-end.

text.p: German call money rates nudged higher to trade around 3.00/3.05 percent on Friday as banks sought more funds in preparation for month-end reserve requirements.

Rates climbed only slightly from Thursday's 2.98/3.00 percent levels but could move higher more quickly on Monday, the last day of the month, dealers predicted. In order to meet reserve requirements, borrowings at the emergency Lombard facility may rise early next week, they added.
"Currently the market appears to be in equilibrium," said one dealer.
Banks held 40.4 billion marks in reserve at the Bundesbank on Thursday, compared with 41.8 billion marks on Wednesday.
Meanwhile the monthly average holdings were unchanged at 38.5 billion marks. Lombard borrowings stood at 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Offered Rate was calculated at 3.08050 percent on Friday compared with 3.04408 percent on Thursday.
